topic: Electric Charge, Current, Voltage and Potential Difference
title: Volts vs Amps Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav's phone charger says 5 V and 2 A. Two numbers on every charger, but what do they really mean? In this animated lesson we build the four basic ideas of electricity from the ground up: electric charge (protons and electrons, like charges repel, charge comes in packets of e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C, Q = ne), electric current (I = Q/t, one ampere is one coulomb per second), and potential difference or voltage (V = W/Q, one volt is one joule per coulomb), explained with two water tanks.

On a live breadboard you watch a cell, a switch and a resistor: the voltmeter reads 1.5 V even with the switch open, but no current flows until the switch closes. Add a second cell and the voltage and current traces on the oscilloscope step up together. Then we derive W = VQ = VIt step by step, work out the charge, energy and number of electrons for one minute of phone charging, and finish with the exam trap (current flows through, voltage is across), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 6 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 2: Principles of Electricity, Network Theorems and AC Principles (Karnataka PUC Electronics).

In this video:
0:00 What do 5 V and 2 A mean?
0:10 Electric charge and Q = ne
0:52 Electric current: I = Q/t
1:20 Potential difference: V = W/Q
1:58 Voltage and current on a breadboard
2:36 Voltage is the push, current is the flow
2:40 Energy from a source: W = VIt
3:00 Worked example: one minute of charging
3:30 Exam trap: through vs across
3:43 Where it is asked
3:55 Practice question
4:28 Formula card
